     one fresh DISAGREE alone             -> gate FAILS (correct)

=== ANOMALY, REPORTED HONESTLY AND NOT CHARGED ===

On my FIRST full-suite run at the new head I got "1 failed, 605 passed", the failure being tests/test_lwb_lanes.py::test_is_record_only_commit_true_for_a_merge_with_empty_first_parent_diff. I then ran the full suite SEVEN more times (606 passed every time) and the test in isolation (1 passed) and the file alone (77 passed). I could not reproduce it once. The failing run was issued in the same shell invocation as the `git reset --hard` that moved me to the new head, which is the most likely explanation (a stale import or a race against the working tree being rewritten), but I did not prove that and I will not assert it.
I am NOT charging this as a defect: one non-reproducing failure in eight runs is not evidence of a broken test, and inventing a fault to look useful is worse than reporting nothing. I record it because a test that fails once and then cannot be reproduced is exactly what a real intermittent looks like early on, and because this particular test guards merge-commit handling -- git-plumbing-shaped behaviour where an environment-sensitive flake would be plausible. Worth watching on the CI matrix; not worth blocking on.

=== OBSERVATIONS, RAISED NOT CHARGED ===

- `_is_stale_only_rejection` matches on the literal substring "STALE" in a free-text error string. The docstring is candid that this is deliberate (to leave `_review_ok`'s signature and its existing tests untouched) and argues correctly that "STALE" appears in exactly one of `_review_ok`'s failure branches and is never combined with another rejection in the same call. I verified the `len(record_errors) == 1` guard makes the combined case safe. It remains a string-keyed coupling between two functions: if a future rejection message ever contains the word "STALE" for another reason, dissent would silently become downgradable again. A structured reason code would be sturdier; the tests (R1/R2) would catch the regression, so this is a robustness note, not a defect.
- `_commit_parents` uses `check=True`, so an unresolvable sha raises rather than returning a value that could be misread as "no parents". That is the right side of this repo's "could not check must not look like checked and found nothing" rule -- named because it was done correctly.
- Treating a merge with an EMPTY first-parent diff as record-only is correct for the `-s ours`/already-identical cases the docstring names. I note without charging that `resolve_reviewable_head` walks `git log` (all ancestors, not `--first-parent`), so after skipping such a merge the walk can land on a commit from the SECOND parent's history. That property is pre-existing, not introduced here, but it interacts with this change and may deserve its own look.
- The merge lane-ownership exemption is not a hole as far as I can reason: commits arriving via a merge that are NOT already in the base are themselves in `commits_in_range` and get lane-checked individually. I reasoned this from the code rather than testing the adversarial case, so I flag it as reasoning, not measurement.

=== NEAR-MISSES OF MY OWN, PRINTED AS REQUIRED ===

THREE, all caught before they became false accusations.

FIRST, and the most serious: I had my round-1 DISAGREE finding written up as a SILENT governance change -- "the PR frames this as a stale-record fix while quietly removing reviewer veto power" -- and was heading for a DISAGREE verdict on that basis. Before filing I went and read the `independent_reviews` docstring I was about to accuse, and it names "wrong verdict" explicitly among the rejections being demoted. The author had documented it in the very diff I was reviewing. My charge of concealment was simply false; what survived was the narrower, accurate point about test coverage and README recording -- and then c04be73 fixed even that. I came close to charging an innocent pull request with hiding something it had written down.

SECOND: I first read the merge commit a25e17e4's first-parent diff as touching only HANDOFF.md, which would have made PR #48's merge look trivially reviewable and would have CONTRADICTED this PR's entire premise. That was my error: I had run `git diff a25e17e4^1 a25e17e4 -- HANDOFF.md`, restricting to one path. Unrestricted it is 31 files. Caught before I drew any conclusion from it.

THIRD: see the ANOMALY section -- I nearly reported a red suite as a defect of this PR on the strength of a single run.

Separately, on PR SELECTION rather than on this PR: my instructions say to skip a PR whose record names the CURRENT HEAD SHA. Applied literally that would have had me re-review all 12 open PRs, because committing a review record advances the raw head, so no record can ever name it. The gate does not work that way -- resolve_reviewable_head skips record-only commits -- and comparing against the REVIEWABLE head shows 10 of 12 were already reviewed at the code they contain. The cost of the literal reading is visible in this repository: reviews/40/ holds SEVEN records and reviews/44/ holds FIVE, all naming a single reviewable head. Reported separately as a defect in the reviewer routine, not in any pull request.
